neighbours.label: the determiner after 'to' that introduces the customer or recipient of a commercial act (sell / advertise / tout to their customers)
fire: Critics argue that theme parks spoil the very scenery that they market to their visitors.
Hotels in the area promote quiet beaches to their guests while building loud bars.
The bakery began selling its bread last winter to a chain of cafés in Leeds.
Phone carriers keep pitching new plans to their subscribers every month.
The brewery shipped its first batch in March to a distributor in Ohio.
Luxury brands advertise exclusivity to their buyers while mass producing goods.
The airline offers cheap upgrades to its passengers on long flights.
Banks often push credit cards to their clients as soon as they turn eighteen.
quiet: Critics argue that theme parks spoil the very scenery that people travel far to see.
Hotels in the area are building loud bars next to the quiet beaches.
The bakery began baking its bread last winter in a new oven in Leeds.
Phone carriers keep changing their plans every month.
The brewery finished its first batch in March after a long delay.
Luxury brands claim exclusivity while mass producing their goods.
The airline upgraded its fleet of planes for long flights.
Banks often raise interest rates as soon as inflation climbs.

notes: Card has no single token (a, their, of, else, path). Probe: 'advertise to their customers' 0.67, 'sale ... to a Swiss utility' 0.18, plain 'gave the book to a friend' 0.04. Weak hypothesis.
